tables.name: users
tables.purpose: Stable user identity; MVP credentials remain hardcoded in the backend.

tables.name: boards
tables.purpose: One board per user; revision tracks both board saves and completed chat turns.
constraints: FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE CASCADE

tables.name: board_columns
tables.purpose: Five fixed slots per board, with editable titles and immutable order.

columns.title: TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(title)) > 0)
columns.position: INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (position BETWEEN 0 AND 4)

constraints: FOREIGN KEY (board_id) REFERENCES boards (id) ON DELETE CASCADE

tables.name: cards
tables.purpose: Editable cards with dense zero-based ordering within each column.
constraints: FOREIGN KEY (board_id, column_id) REFERENCES board_columns (board_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE

tables.name: chat_messages
tables.purpose: Persist completed user/assistant turns in deterministic conversation order.
constraints: FOREIGN KEY (board_id) REFERENCES boards (id) ON DELETE CASCADE

identity.columns: Existing fixed col-* IDs, scoped to a board.
identity.cards: Preserve existing card-1 through card-8 for seeds. New manual cards use client-generated crypto.randomUUID() IDs; new AI cards use backend-generated UUIDs.
identity.messages: Server-generated UUID strings, scoped to a board.
identity.turns: Client-generated UUID reused when retrying the same chat request.

application_invariants: Each board has exactly the five fixed column IDs in the specified order. Only titles can change.
Each card occurs in exactly one column and cardIds ordering matches stored positions.
All card and column queries include board_id resolved from the authenticated user.
Column titles and card titles are trimmed and nonempty. Empty card details are allowed.
Card positions are dense zero-based integers after each committed board save.
A completed chat turn contains exactly one user message and one assistant message, inserted atomically.
Every accepted board save or completed chat turn increments the board revision once.
Only a new board is seeded. Reloads, sign-ins, empty boards, and container restarts never reseed it.
